title: Compatibility of coefficient restriction with tensor pullback
statement: For the same schemes, coefficient sheaves, coefficient isomorphism and three signed-total tensor models as [lem-pbc-coefficient-restriction-tensor-chain-square] and [def-sfb-proetale-tensor-model], there exists a restriction tensor isomorphism rho compatible with the canonical geometric tensor comparisons and the canonical restriction/pullback comparison b. Explicitly, for all derived F,G, b at aY(F,G) followed by alpha_i(F,G) equals U(alpha_c(F,G)) followed by rho inverse at (L_c F,L_c G) and z(b_F,b_G). Unlike the old signature, rho is constructed with its chain normalization and b is fixed to the canonical comparison. The canonical b and its termwise normalization are defined in [lem-pbc-coefficient-pullback-factorization].

proof.text: Apply ringIso_tensor_transport to c. Its flat_iff and kflat_iff clauses preserve flat-term K-flat representatives. Its totalIso and total_naturality fields supply the normalized chain tensor isomorphism. The chain-square lemma compares this map with the two ordinary geometric tensor pullbacks.

Apply tensorComparisonDescent to exact restriction, sigma and the two target tensor-model representatives. Fully faithful restriction to flat K-flat representatives supplies the descent hypothesis. Obtain gamma, and take rho=gamma inverse.

Apply the proved representative_square to the descended gamma and its normalization. This computes the canonical geometric square on every flat K-flat pair. Reflect equality of the resulting natural transformations through fully faithful restriction to those resolving representatives.

lean.statement:
theorem tensorComparison_compatibility {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (R : Sheaf (ProEt.topology Y) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (S : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (c : (proEtaleSheafInverseImage f CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj R ≅ S)
    (aY : ProEtaleTensorModel Y R)
    (z : ProEtaleTensorModel X
      ((proEtaleSheafInverseImage f CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj R))
    (aX : ProEtaleTensorModel X S) :
    ∃ rho : ((pbcDerivedRestrict c.hom).prod (pbcDerivedRestrict c.hom)) ⋙ z.tensor ≅
        aX.tensor ⋙ pbcDerivedRestrict c.hom,
      ∀ F G : DerivedCategory (proEtaleRingModules Y R),
        (pullback f R S c).hom.app (aY.tensor.obj (F, G)) ≫
            (proEtaleCanonicalTensorComparison f R
              ((proEtaleSheafInverseImage f CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj R)
              (Iso.refl _) aY z).hom.app (F, G) =
          (pbcDerivedRestrict c.hom).map
              ((proEtaleCanonicalTensorComparison f R S c aY aX).hom.app (F, G)) ≫
            rho.inv.app ((proEtaleRingDerivedPullback f R S c).obj F,
              (proEtaleRingDerivedPullback f R S c).obj G) ≫
            z.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom
              ((pullback f R S c).hom.app F)
              ((pullback f R S c).hom.app G))

statement_change.old_statement: Given the normalized restriction tensor isomorphism and the canonical coefficient pullback comparison, the two induced maps on every pair of derived objects are equal.
statement_change.what: The old Lean signature universally quantified unnormalized rho and b. Negating rho alone negates just the right-hand side; on integer tensor units this contradicts invertibility. The corrected source statement constructs a normalized rho and fixes the canonical b. The original parent goal is unchanged.

old_proof.text: Evaluate both composites on flat K-flat representatives. The canonical geometric tensor comparisons and restriction/pullback map pure tensors to the same inverse-image section with its scalar action transported by the coefficient isomorphism.
The equality survives sheafification, signed totalization, localization and descent in both variables, so it holds for arbitrary derived objects.
